citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines nonmedical home health services (home health aide services, personal care services incl. self-administration help), direct care, nonagency provider (not more than 2 unrelated individuals excluded) and immediate family member.

citations.title: License requirements
citations.requirement: An agency or nonagency provider may not provide, or hold itself out as providing, nonmedical home health services without a current nonmedical or skilled license.

citations.title: Applications for licensure (nonmedical)
citations.requirement: Application: owner fingerprints, SOS filings, notarized identity affidavit, criminal records check policy, days/hours, services and policies, service area, $20,000 bond if new, $250 fee. Waiver if ODA-certified (B)(3).

citations.title: Issuance of licenses
citations.requirement: ODH reviews each application. It issues the license once the fee is paid and the ORC 3740.03 requirements are shown, unless 3740.07 applies. A site visit is mandated only for the Medicare-certification basis.

citations.title: Validity, renewal of licenses
citations.requirement: License is valid three years. Renewal requires the $250 renewal fee and a showing of continued compliance with ORC 3740.03. ODH may adjust the initial renewal date.

citations.title: Enforcement
citations.requirement: ODH may refuse to issue or renew, limit, suspend or revoke a license, or impose probation or reprimand. Actions follow ORC Chapter 119.

citations.title: Rules
citations.requirement: Director of Health adopts rules on application and renewal forms and procedures, grounds for enforcement, and dispute resolution/appeals, in consultation with ODA and the Medicaid Director.

citations.title: Criminal records check
citations.requirement: Agency may not employ direct-care applicants or employees who appear in the listed databases or have disqualifying offenses. Requires database review and BCI check. Conditional hire allowed if the check is requested within 5 business days. Reports are confidential.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines direct care, disqualifying information, nonmedical home health services and personal care services. Para (Y) lists what staff may do for self-administration of medication (remind, hand, open container, assist).

citations.title: Applicability
citations.requirement: Since Oct 1, 2022, no provider may deliver or advertise nonmedical home health services without a license. Violation is a 2nd-degree misdemeanor on a first offense and a 1st-degree misdemeanor for each later offense.

citations.title: Nonmedical license application contents
citations.requirement: Complete application: prescribed forms, $250 non-refundable fee (cashier's check or money order), owners/officers, services list and related policies, SOS documents, written criminal records check policy, hours, area, fingerprints, $20,000 bond.

citations.title: ODH information requests, renewal timing, change notice, term
citations.requirement: Reply to ODH information requests within 14 days of mailing. Renewal is timely if filed at least 90 days before expiration. Give ODH written notice within 10 days of any application change. License lasts 3 years.

citations.title: Enforcement
citations.requirement: Director may deny, suspend or revoke for material misrepresentation, failure to timely renew, or no longer meeting requirements. Hearing right under ORC 119. Informal dispute resolution is available after a denial.

citations.title: State and national database review
citations.requirement: Before the criminal records check, check SAM, OIG LEIE, DODD abuse registry, sex offender database, ODRC inmate database and Ohio nurse aide registry for each direct-care applicant and employee. Disqualifying information bars employment.

citations.title: Requirements for criminal records check
citations.requirement: BCI check of each direct-care applicant; employees rechecked within 30 days after each 5-year hire anniversary. FBI check if not an Ohio resident for 5 years. Applicant notice, fee rules and fingerprint forms are specified.

citations.title: Conditional employment
citations.requirement: Conditional hire only if the database review is clear, fingerprints are submitted before start, and the check is requested within 5 business days. Terminate if results are not received within 60 days or show a disqualifying offense.

citations.title: Disqualifying offenses; personal character standards
citations.requirement: 3701-60-07(D) says 3701-60-08(A) lists the offenses that bar direct-care employment and 3701-60-09 lets an agency employ a person anyway. Rule text itself was not fetched; read before drafting.

citations.title: ODA certification: requirements to become certified
citations.requirement: Business site with locked record storage accessible to ODA/ODM/HHS/Auditor. $1M commercial liability insurance covering theft/property damage, plus written instructions for loss claims. Written incident policy. EVV. Email/phone on file.

citations.title: ODA certified provider reporting duties
citations.requirement: Report suspected abuse/neglect/exploitation to APS and notify ODA or its designee within 1 business day. Report significant changes within 1 business day. Report contact changes within 7 days. Give 30 days' written notice before ending service, with exceptions.

citations.title: ODA confidentiality and ethical/professional standards
citations.requirement: Comply with confidentiality laws (HIPAA 45 CFR 160/162/164, 42 CFR 431.300-307). Prohibits gifts or tips, sexual conduct, alcohol or drugs, distractions, sleeping, visitors, selling to clients, social media photos without consent.

citations.title: ODA records retention, access, payment, rule updates
citations.requirement: Keep service records 6 years after payment (or until review/audit ends) and qualification records for employment plus 6 years. Give ODA/ODM/HHS/Auditor immediate access. Accept the agreed rate as payment in full. Subscribe to ODA rule emails.

citations.title: ODA agency provider disclosures, attestations, policies
citations.requirement: Agencies disclose owners (and any felony convictions) and an organization table, and show an active SOS registration. They attest to 45 CFR 80.4, EEO, wage-hour and workers' comp compliance, and tax payment. Written policies must require staff to meet (B)(8) conduct standards.

citations.title: ODA personal care: definition and provider types
citations.requirement: Personal care is hands-on ADL/IADL help, home management, help with self-administration of medications, homemaker tasks and errands, as authorized in the service plan. Respite is excluded. Providers are ODA-certified agencies or participant-directed providers.

citations.title: ODA personal care: availability and staffing
citations.requirement: Accept a referral only with adequate PCA and PCA-supervisor staffing for the authorized hours. An RN or LPN supervises PCAs during all scheduled hours. Maintain a back-up plan for when no PCA or supervisor is available.

citations.title: ODA personal care: initial PCA qualifications
citations.requirement: PCA must be an STNA, meet Medicare HHA standards, have 1 year of supervised aide experience plus competency evaluation, complete COALA or a vocational program, or complete a 30-hour program covering the listed topics.

citations.title: ODA personal care: orientation, in-service, verification
citations.requirement: Orientation before any in-person client contact (7 listed topics). Six hours of ODA-approved in-service every 12 months (orientation excluded). Keep training certificates, nurse aide registry printout, and prior-employment proof.

citations.title: ODA personal care: PCA supervisors and visits
citations.requirement: Only an RN or LPN under RN direction may supervise. In-person home visit and activity plan before or at the first episode. Follow-up visit at least every 60 days; at least two in-person visits a year, with the rest allowed by phone or video. Visits are documented.

citations.title: ODA personal care: policies and service verification
citations.requirement: Written policies on job descriptions and on records showing each PCA's qualifications. Per episode, keep date, arrival and departure times, activities, PCA name and ID, and client ID. Subject to Chapter 5160-32 EVV and ORC 121.36.

citations.title: Ohio Home Care Waiver personal care aide: scope and medication
citations.requirement: Services follow the PCSP and are limited to the approved hours. Aides do not administer prescribed or OTC medications. They may only help with self-administration: remind, hand the container, open it, assist the physically impaired.

citations.title: Ohio Home Care Waiver personal care aide: provider and aide requirements
citations.requirement: Agency aides must be employed by a Medicare-certified or accredited agency. They need an ODH/Medicare competency certificate, first aid, 8 in-service hours a year, and RN/LPN home visits every 60 days. Non-agency aides complete 6 in-service hours.

citations.title: Ohio Home Care Waiver personal care aide: clinical record
citations.requirement: Confidential clinical record at the place of business. Contents: ID data, PCSP, allergies and dietary restrictions, advance directives, task log with times and dated signatures, signed progress notes, and a discharge summary.

citations.title: ODM waiver provider conditions of participation
citations.requirement: Active Medicaid agreement; staff age 18+; written acknowledgment of 5160-44-05 on enrollment and yearly; new-provider training within 90 days; HIPAA and 42 CFR 431 compliance; contact updates within 7 days; back-up plan; 72-hour notice of planned absence.

citations.title: ODM waiver: visit documentation and retention
citations.requirement: Document each visit: tasks done or not done, date, location, start and end times, and provider and client signatures (client signature within 3 business days if not obtained at the visit). Keep service and billing records 6 years from payment or until audit ends.

citations.title: ODM waiver: 24-hour notices and termination of service
citations.requirement: Notify ODM or its designee within 24 hours of changes in client condition, environment, caregiver, move, refusals, threats, or safety concerns. Give 30 days' written notice before ending service (10 days after hospital, institution or jail).

citations.title: ODM waiver: EVV, prohibited conduct, legal decision-makers
citations.requirement: Personal care visits must be verified by ODM-approved EVV. Prohibits abuse, gifts or loans, falsifying signatures, billing while the client is hospitalized, sleeping, visitors, impairment, and acting as POA or guardian.

citations.title: HCBS waiver incident management
citations.requirement: Providers take immediate protective action and report any incident to the case management agency immediately, and no later than 1 business day. Defines critical incidents (abuse, neglect, exploitation, medication error, death, missing) and required report contents.

citations.title: Person-centered planning (HCBS)
citations.requirement: The individual leads planning. The service plan must be in plain language, accessible to LEP and disabled persons, signed, and distributed. It includes back-up plans and is reviewed at least every 12 months, on significant change, or on request.

citations.title: Older Americans Act: personal care
citations.requirement: Staffing adequate for personal care at least 5 days a week. Back-up plan when no aide is available. Supervisor available during scheduled hours. Aide qualifications and 6 hours of ODA-approved in-service per 12 months.

citations.title: Ohio Home Care Waiver billing and covered services
citations.requirement: Sets billing and reimbursement for Ohio Home Care Waiver services, including personal care aide units. Read the current text (effective Apr 17, 2026) before billing.

citations.title: Ohio Home Care Waiver: home care attendant
citations.requirement: Home care attendant service (S5125) rate and billing rules; includes nursing-task component outside nonmedical scope. Applies only if the agency enrolls for that service.

citations.title: Medicaid personal care aide service (EVV-covered, T1019)
citations.requirement: Personal care aide service under HCPCS T1019 is subject to Electronic Visit Verification. Per ODM, EVV captures service type, recipient, date, location, worker and start/end time.

citations.title: PASSPORT eligibility and enrollment
citations.requirement: PASSPORT enrollment requires an open slot within the CMS-authorized limit. Providers accept referrals only for enrolled, authorized individuals.

citations.title: Electronic visit verification rules (cross-referenced)
citations.requirement: OAC 173-39-02(A)(8) and 173-39-02.11(C)(6)(b) say Chapter 5160-32 (and 5160-1-40 before 7/1/2024) sets EVV system requirements. Chapter text was not fetched; read before writing EVV procedures.

citations.title: Mandatory reporting of adult abuse, neglect, exploitation (cross-referenced)
citations.requirement: OAC 173-39-02(B)(3)(a) says this section requires reporting of reasonable cause to believe an individual suffered abuse, neglect or exploitation to local APS. Statute text was not fetched; confirm the reporter list and timing.

citations.title: Direct-care worker relationships eligible for payment (cross-referenced)
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced in 173-39-02(B)(5) and 5160-44-31 as setting which relatives and legal decision-makers may be paid direct-care workers. Rule text was not fetched.

citations.title: ODM provider monitoring, review and oversight (cross-referenced)
citations.requirement: 5160-44-31(B)(2)(d) and (B)(16) require cooperation with ODM monitoring under these rules. Text was not fetched.

citations.title: HIPAA and Medicaid safeguarding of applicant/recipient information
citations.requirement: HIPAA applies to Medicaid-billing providers. ODA rule 173-39-02(B)(4) and ODM rule 5160-44-31(B)(12) require compliance. Federal text was not fetched in this step; the state rules incorporating it were.

citations.title: OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard
citations.requirement: Applies to employees with occupational exposure to blood or OPIM. Requires exposure control plan, training, PPE and sharps controls. Federal text was not fetched in this step.

citations.title: HCBS settings requirements (cross-referenced)
citations.requirement: OAC 173-39-02(A)(3)(b) subjects provider business sites to the HCBS setting rules in 5160-44-01. Rule text was not fetched.

citations.cite: Ohio Const. Art. II §34a; ORC Chapter 4111; Ohio Dept. of Commerce 2026 minimum wage notice
citations.title: Ohio minimum wage and poster
citations.requirement: 2026 Ohio minimum wage is $11.00/hour for non-tipped employees. It applies to employers above $405,000 gross receipts; smaller employers stay at the federal floor. Employers must display the official 2026 poster.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
state_specifics: The agency is licensed by ODH as a nonmedical home health services provider (ORC 3740.02).
The rules reviewed set no administrator qualifications, so the manual names the administrator and confirms the standard with ODH in writing.
Owners and officers are disclosed to ODH, and to ODA if the agency is certified; felony convictions are disclosed to ODA.
The agency keeps an active Ohio Secretary of State registration and files its SOS documents with the ODH application.

policies.title: Licensure, Advertising and Surety Bond Requirements
state_specifics: No services may be provided or advertised without a current ODH license (OAC 3701-60-02).
Penalty for operating unlicensed: 2nd-degree misdemeanor on a first offense, 1st-degree on each later offense.
The license term is 3 years and the renewal fee is $250.
A new provider posts a $20,000 surety bond issued by a surety licensed in Ohio.
Use the exact licensed legal name and state 'licensed by the Ohio Department of Health' only after issuance.

policies.title: Services List, Days and Hours of Operation and Geographic Service Area
state_specifics: The ODH application must contain a list of nonmedical services provided and the related policies and procedures.
It must also contain a statement of days and hours of operation and a description of the geographic area served.
Services are limited to the nonmedical scope in ORC 3740.01 and OAC 3701-60-01; no skilled or medical services.
The manual keeps the current statement as an appendix, updated on any change (see GOV-07).

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Written policies are developed, implemented, followed and maintained on the OAC 173-39-02.11(C)(5) topics (job descriptions, PCA qualification records).
Review the manual at least annually, and whenever a rule changes.
Subscribe to ODA rule-update emails (OAC 173-39-02(B)(13)) and monitor OAC Chapter 3701-60 (next five-year review 01/27/2028).
Keep a dated version history and staff acknowledgments.

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: Audit monthly: criminal records and database screening status, in-service hours, supervisory visits, EVV/visit records, and incident reports.
Track missed visits, complaints, incidents and abuse/neglect reports, and review them with the administrator.
Corrective actions are documented and closed within 30 days.
The 30-day close-out and audit frequency are agency policy, not rule.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Accept the agreed rate as payment in full from Medicaid and ODA programs.
Never bill while a client is hospitalized, and never falsify client signatures or visit times (OAC 5160-44-31).
Cooperate with ODM monitoring and reviews (OAC 5160-45-06 and -09 are cross-references; read before relying).
ODM is increasing payment suspensions and program-integrity actions; keep complete time, EVV, supervision and screening records.
Check ODM's moratorium and enrollment status (May 14 to Nov 14, 2026 for home health provider types) before any Medicaid enrollment.

policies.title: ODH License Renewal, Change Notices and Enforcement
state_specifics: Give ODH written notice within 10 days of any change to application information (owner, address, name, services, hours, area, bond).
Reply to ODH information requests within 14 days of the mailing date.
File the renewal at least 90 days before expiration; calendar a reminder 120 days out.
ODH may deny, limit, suspend, revoke, or place on probation; the hearing right is under ORC Chapter 119, and informal dispute resolution is available after a denial.
One named person sends notices and keeps proof of delivery.

policies.title: Insurance, Surety Bond and Theft or Property Damage Loss Claims
state_specifics: Keep the $20,000 ODH surety bond continuously in force.
For ODA-certified services, carry $1M commercial liability insurance covering theft and property damage.
Give any individual written instructions on how to obtain payment for loss due to theft or property damage by the agency or its employees.
Hand out the instructions at intake and keep a signed receipt.

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: The individual leads planning and makes choices about services.
Written rights are in plain language and available in other languages and accessible formats.
For Medicaid HCBS clients, the individual's choice, privacy and dignity are respected in the home setting (OAC 5160-44-01 is a cross-reference; read before relying).
Provide the rights statement at intake and get a signed acknowledgment.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Accept complaints orally or in writing, without retaliation.
Acknowledge a complaint within 2 business days and resolve it within 14 days.
The 2-day and 14-day periods are agency policy, not rule.
Tell clients they may also contact their case management agency or ODA/ODM, and ODH about licensure concerns.
Log every complaint and its outcome.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Criminal records check reports are confidential (ORC 3740.11).
Do not post photos or information about clients on social media without written consent.
Release client information only with authorization or as law permits.

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Staff may not accept gifts, tips, loans or purchases from clients, nor sell to or buy from them.
Staff may not use a client's food or property, or act as the client's POA or guardian (OAC 5160-44-31).
Staff may not handle client money except as in the written service plan, with receipts.
Suspected exploitation is reported under SAF-01.
Relatives' eligibility as paid workers follows OAC 5160-44-32 (cross-reference; read before relying).

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: An ODA-certified agency attests compliance with 45 CFR 80.4 and EEO laws.
Service plans and notices must be accessible to people with limited English proficiency and to people with disabilities.
Provide interpreter or translation help at no cost.
Do not refuse service because of race, color, national origin, disability, age, sex or religion.

policies.title: Service Agreement, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: The private-pay agreement states the hourly rate, minimum visit length, cancellation terms, billing cycle, scope, and that caregivers do not administer medications.
For Medicaid and ODA clients, the agreed rate is payment in full and the client is not balance-billed.
Give the 30-day notice of service end (see SVC-11).
Give a copy to the client and keep the signed original in the record.

policies.title: Scope of Services - What Caregivers May and May Not Do
state_specifics: Allowed: hands-on help with ADLs and IADLs, home management, homemaker tasks and errands, and help with self-administration of medication, as authorized in the plan.
Not allowed: nursing or skilled tasks, or administering prescribed or OTC medication (OAC 5160-46-04).
Caregivers do only tasks in the service plan, within authorized hours.
Respite is excluded from ODA personal care (OAC 173-39-02.11(A)).
Job descriptions mirror this scope (see PER-03).

policies.title: Client Intake, Eligibility and Assessment
state_specifics: Accept a referral only with adequate PCA and PCA supervisor staffing for the authorized hours.
Complete an in-home assessment before or at the first service episode.
Medicaid and PASSPORT clients must be enrolled and authorized (OAC 5160-31-03); an open slot is required.
Screen out needs outside nonmedical scope and refer them.
Document the staffing check on the intake form.

policies.title: Service Plan and Plan Updates
state_specifics: The plan is in plain language, signed and distributed to the client.
It includes a back-up plan, allergies, dietary restrictions and advance directives.
Review at least every 12 months, on significant change, or on request.
Services follow the plan and the approved hours.

policies.title: Supervisory Visits
state_specifics: Initial in-person home visit before or at the first episode to define expected activities and develop a written or electronic activity plan.
Follow-up visits at least every 60 days.
Phone or video visits are allowed only if at least 2 in-person visits occur per year.
Each visit is documented in the client's record.
OAC 5160-46-04 separately requires an RN/LPN home visit every 60 days for Home Care Waiver agency aides.

policies.title: PCA Supervisor Qualifications and Supervision Coverage
state_specifics: Only an RN, or an LPN under the direction of an RN, may be the PCA supervisor.
An RN or LPN supervises PCAs during all hours PCAs are scheduled to work.
ODH rules reviewed set no supervisor credential for private pay; the agency applies the RN/LPN standard to all clients as one uniform policy.
Verify the supervisor's license and keep it in the personnel file.
Publish the supervisor's on-call contact for every scheduled shift.

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
state_specifics: Staff may only remind, hand the container, open it, and assist a physically impaired client (OAC 3701-60-01(Y); OAC 5160-46-04).
Staff may not administer prescribed or OTC medications.
A medication error is a critical incident reportable under OAC 5160-44-05 (see SAF-02).
Record assistance in the task log.

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: A failure to provide an authorized service at the authorized time is a significant change to be reported within 1 business day (see SVC-14).
Give 72 hours' notice of a planned absence (OAC 5160-44-31).
For Older Americans Act personal care, staffing must cover at least 5 days a week.
Log every missed visit with its reason and make-up plan.

policies.title: Back-Up Plan for Caregiver or Supervisor Unavailability
state_specifics: Maintain a written back-up plan for providing personal care when no PCA or PCA supervisor is available.
Back-up plans are also written into each client's service plan.
Keep trained back-up caregivers and an on-call rotation.
Notify the client, and the case manager for Medicaid clients, of any gap.

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Service Verification
state_specifics: For each episode keep: service date, PCA arrival and departure times, activities, name and unique ID of each PCA, and unique client ID.
EVV is required for Medicaid personal care (T1019) and captures service type, recipient, date, location, worker and start/end time (ODM's Sandata is free).
Follow OAC Chapter 5160-32 and ORC 121.36 (Chapter 5160-32 text not fetched; read before finalizing).
Client signature is due within 3 business days if not obtained at the visit.
Never alter or falsify visit times; manual edits need documented reasons.

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: In an emergency call 911 first, then the supervisor.
Notify ODM or its designee within 24 hours of changes in client condition, environment, caregiver, move, refusals, threats or safety concerns (OAC 5160-44-31(B)(17)).
Incidents are reported under SAF-02.
Document the event and notify the family or representative.

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Discontinuation of Services
state_specifics: Give the individual and ODA's designee written notice at least 30 days before the last day of service (OAC 173-39-02(B)(3)(d)), except in the listed circumstances.
ODM waiver: 30 days' written notice, or 10 days after hospital, institution or jail.
Immediate safety situations are handled under the exceptions and reported.
Complete a discharge summary and help with transition to another provider.

policies.title: Coordination with Medicaid Programs and Payers
state_specifics: Pathways: ODA PASSPORT (OAC 173-39) and Ohio Home Care Waiver (OAC 5160-46).
Enrollment, rates and referral rules must be confirmed with ODM and the Council on Aging before billing.
Acknowledge OAC 5160-44-05 in writing at enrollment and yearly (OAC 5160-44-31).
Complete new-provider training within 90 days of ODM enrollment.
Report contact changes to ODM or its designee within 7 days.

policies.title: Ohio Home Care Waiver Personal Care Aide Requirements
state_specifics: Applies only if the agency enrolls with ODM; many requirements go beyond ODH licensure.
Agency aides need an ODH/Medicare competency certificate, first aid, and 8 hours of in-service per year (non-agency aides: 6 hours).
RN/LPN home visits at least every 60 days.
The agency must be Medicare-certified or otherwise accredited (OAC 5160-46-04(E)).
The home care attendant service (S5125) includes nursing tasks outside nonmedical scope; do not provide it unless separately enrolled.

policies.title: Significant Change Notices to ODA or Case Management Agency
state_specifics: Notify ODA or its designee no later than 1 business day after learning of a significant change.

Triggers: (i) an authorized service not provided at the authorized time, (ii) the individual moves, (iii) repeated refusal of services, (iv) any incident under OAC 5160-44-05, (v) any other significant change in status or environment.
Use the notice form and keep proof of transmission.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Report any reasonable cause to believe abuse, neglect or exploitation to the local county APS program under ORC 5101.63 (statute text not fetched; confirm reporter list and timing).
Also notify ODA or its designee within 1 business day (OAC 173-39-02(B)(3)(a)).
Take immediate protective action; report the incident to the case management agency immediately and no later than 1 business day (OAC 5160-44-05).
Staff may not abuse or neglect clients (OAC 5160-44-31).
Post the county APS number in the office; use the APS log.

policies.title: Incident Reporting
state_specifics: A written or electronic policy on documenting incidents is required (OAC 173-39-02(A)(7)).
Critical incidents include abuse, neglect, exploitation, medication error, death and missing person (OAC 5160-44-05).
Report to the case management agency immediately, no later than 1 business day, using the required report contents.
Staff complete the incident report within 24 hours of the incident (agency policy).

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Orientation must cover standard precautions for infection control before any in-person client contact.
Provide gloves and PPE and train staff on handwashing, linen and waste handling.
Staff with communicable illness do not work with clients.
Follow current CDC and ODH guidance.

policies.title: Bloodborne Pathogens Exposure Control
state_specifics: OSHA applies where employees have occupational exposure to blood or OPIM.
The agency conducts an exposure determination and, if exposure is anticipated, keeps a written exposure control plan.
Provide training, PPE and sharps handling instructions; offer hepatitis B vaccine where required.
Federal text not fetched in the research; confirm before finalizing.

policies.title: Client Emergency and Disaster Plans
state_specifics: Each client's plan identifies emergency contacts, evacuation needs and medical vulnerabilities.
The back-up plan applies during severe weather and disasters.
The agency tests its on-call line.
Staff orientation covers emergency procedures (OAC 173-39-02.11(C)(3)(b)(vi)).

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: Threats and safety concerns are reported to ODM or its designee within 24 hours (OAC 5160-44-31).
Staff may leave an unsafe home and notify the supervisor immediately.
Staff report firearms, hostile persons and unsafe conditions.
Document the incident (see SAF-02).

policies.title: Transporting Clients
state_specifics: Errands are covered as authorized in the service plan; client transport requires written authorization in the plan.
Staff driving must hold a valid license and insurance.
Carry hired and non-owned auto coverage.
Staff may not take the client to the business site (OAC 173-39-02(B)(8)).

policies.title: Caregiver Qualifications and Certification
state_specifics: A PCA must be one of: STNA, Medicare HHA standards, 1 year of supervised aide experience plus competency evaluation, COALA or a vocational program, or a 30-hour program covering the listed topics.
Staff must be age 18 or older (OAC 5160-44-31).
Home Care Waiver agency aides need an ODH/Medicare competency certificate and first aid.
ODA's 2024 comment package referenced a proposed 30-hour requirement under RC 173.525; confirm current text with ODA.

policies.title: Verification and Records of PCA Qualifications
state_specifics: Keep certificates of completion, or record the school or organization, course name, dates and hours.
Keep the nurse aide registry search results for STNAs.
For the experience pathway keep prior-employment records.
Maintain a written policy on retaining records of how each PCA meets (C)(3) (OAC 173-39-02.11(C)(5)(b)).
Qualification records are kept for employment plus 6 years.

policies.title: Job Descriptions
state_specifics: Each position (administrator, supervisor, scheduler, PCA) has a written job description.
PCA descriptions list only tasks within the nonmedical scope.
The supervisor description requires an RN or LPN license.
Staff sign receipt at hire and on any revision.

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries (Written Criminal Records Check Policy)
state_specifics: This is the written criminal records check policy submitted with the ODH application.
Before the criminal check, review SAM, OIG LEIE, the DODD abuse registry, the sex offender database, the ODRC inmate database and the Ohio nurse aide registry.
Disqualifying information bars employment in direct care.
Screen every direct-care applicant before first client contact.
Reports are confidential.

policies.title: Criminal Records Check Procedure: BCI Requests, Notice and Forms
state_specifics: The chief administrator or designee requests that the BCI superintendent check each applicant for a direct-care position.
Notify the applicant or employee that fingerprints are required and tell them of any fees.
Provide the prescribed forms and fingerprint sheet or instructions, collect the completed forms and forward them to the superintendent.
An applicant or employee who does not complete the forms or provide fingerprints is not employed in a position requiring a check.

policies.title: Five-Year Rechecks and FBI Residency Requirements
state_specifics: Recheck direct-care employees no later than 30 days after the fifth hire anniversary and at least every 5 years.
Employees hired before 1/1/2008: no later than 30 days after the anniversary of hire and at least every 5 years.
If an applicant cannot show 5 years of Ohio residency or an FBI check within that period, request FBI information.
The agency may request FBI information even when the residency test is met.

policies.title: BCI Fees, Reverification and Employment-Service Exception
state_specifics: The agency pays BCI the prescribed fee per check.
It may charge the applicant up to that amount only with notice at initial application and where Medicaid does not reimburse.
A check completed within the previous 12 months may be requested and accepted (reverification).
No new check is needed for an applicant referred by an employment service that confirms database review and a criminal check within 1 year, both showing no disqualifying offense.

policies.title: Conditional Employment and Disqualifying Offenses
state_specifics: Conditional hire only if the database review is clear, fingerprints are submitted before start, and the check is requested within 5 business days.
Terminate if results are not received within 60 days or show a disqualifying offense.
Disqualifying offenses are in OAC 3701-60-08(A), and 3701-60-09 sets when an agency may employ anyway (text not fetched; read before drafting).
Remove from direct care immediately anyone who becomes disqualified.

policies.title: Orientation of Caregivers
state_specifics: Complete orientation before any direct in-person client contact.

Topics: (i) provider's expectations of employees, (ii) ethical standards under OAC 173-39-02, (iii) personnel policies overview, (iv) organization and lines of communication, (v) incident-reporting procedures, (vi) emergency procedures, (vii) standard precautions for infection control.
Keep a signed orientation checklist.

policies.title: Competency Evaluation and Additional Training
state_specifics: Provide additional training and a competency evaluation if the PCA will perform activities not previously trained or evaluated.
Do not assign the task until the evaluation is passed and documented.

policies.title: Annual In-Service Training
state_specifics: Each PCA completes 6 hours of ODA-approved in-service every 12 months (ORC 173.525).
Agency and program-specific orientation do not count toward the 6 hours.
Home Care Waiver agency aides need 8 in-service hours per year.
Track hours in a log and pay for training time as wage-hour law requires.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: The rules reviewed set no specific TB screening requirement for nonmedical agencies; the agency sets a health screen policy and checks with ODH.
Staff with communicable illness are excluded from client contact.
Keep health records in a file separate from personnel records.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Keep qualification records for the period of employment plus 6 years.
File contains: application, screening results, qualification proof, orientation, in-service log, job description and conduct acknowledgment.
Give ODA, ODM, HHS and the Auditor immediate access to records.
Criminal records reports are kept confidential.

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
state_specifics: 2026 Ohio minimum wage is $11.00 per hour for non-tipped employees; it applies to employers above $405,000 gross receipts, and smaller employers stay at the federal floor.
Display the official 2026 minimum wage poster.
Pay for travel time between clients and for overtime as required.
ODA-certified agencies attest to wage-hour and workers' compensation compliance.
Register with Ohio BWC and ODJFS before the first payroll.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: OAC 173-39-02(B)(8)(a)-(n) bars: alcohol or drugs, gifts and tips, sexual conduct, leaving the home, distracting activities, abuse or distress including social media photos, personal relationships, decision-making roles, selling to or buying from the client, use of the client's food or property, taking the client to the business site, and conflicts of interest.
Written policies require employees to comply with (B)(8).
OAC 5160-44-31 also bars sleeping on duty, visitors, impairment, and acting as POA or guardian.
Staff sign the conduct standards at hire and yearly.

policies.title: Supervision of Volunteers
state_specifics: The agency supervises any volunteers it uses.
Volunteers do not provide hands-on personal care unless qualified.
Volunteers sign confidentiality and conduct agreements; apply screening as set in PER-04.

policies.title: Client Records and Retention
state_specifics: Keep service records 6 years after payment and until reviews and audits are resolved.
Keep qualification records for the period of certification or employment plus 6 years.
Home Care Waiver clinical record at the place of business: ID data, PCSP, allergies and dietary restrictions, advance directives, task log, signed progress notes and discharge summary.
Each visit record shows tasks done or not done, date, location, start and end times, and signatures.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Notify ODA or its designee within 7 days of any change in telephone, mailing address or email address.
Notify ODH in writing within 10 days of any change in application information.
ODM also requires contact updates within 7 days.
Abuse, neglect and significant-change reports are due within 1 business day (see SAF-01 and SVC-14).
Keep a reporting calendar and proof of delivery.

policies.title: Business Site, Record Security and Regulator Access
state_specifics: Maintain a business site with locked record storage accessible to ODA, ODM, HHS and the Auditor.
Give regulators immediate access to records.
Keep an email address and phone number on file with ODA or its designee.
Use access controls and backups for electronic records.

documents.title: OAC 3701-60-03 Initial license application, application process, and renewal of license (paragraph (B): nonmedical home health services license)
documents.form_number: OAC 3701-60-03(B). The ODH 'Nonmedical Home Health Services License Application' PDF accompanies it, but I could not open the PDF because its URL was too long for the fetch tool.
documents.issuer: Ohio Department of Health (ODH), Home Health Agency Licensure
documents.how_used: ODH publishes no separate policy checklist for the nonmedical license. This rule lists what a complete application must contain, so I used it as the controlling list. Only the policy and plan items are extracted: (B)(3)(d), (g), (h) and (i). Under (E), items (B)(3)(d) to (k) are waived if the provider shows ODA certification under ORC 173.391. Under (F), items (B)(3)(d) to (i) are waived if the provider shows accreditation by an approved national organization.

documents.title: OAC 3701-60-06 Requirements for criminal records check
documents.how_used: Rule 3701-60-03(B)(3)(g) requires a copy of the agency's written criminal records check policy. This rule sets the content that policy has to follow. It does not list the policy items itself, so the items below are the rule's own duties on the chief administrator.

documents.title: OAC 173-39-02 ODA provider certification: requirements for providers to become, and to remain, certified
documents.how_used: This is the general ODA certification rule for PASSPORT agency providers. It is the regulation section that lists required written policies and reporting duties for agency providers. Only policy-type items are extracted.

documents.title: OAC 173-39-02.11 ODA provider certification: personal care
documents.version: Effective July 1, 2024. The page was last updated August 28, 2025.
documents.how_used: This is the service-specific rule for PASSPORT personal care. Paragraph (C)(5) 'Provider policies' is the closest thing to an enumerated policy list. I also extracted the staffing, orientation, training, supervision and service-verification duties that a policy manual must address.

required_items.text: A list of the nonmedical home health services which are or will be provided by the home health agency or nonagency provider and any policies and procedures related to those services, if applicable.
If the applicant for licensure is a home health agency, a copy of the home health agency's written criminal records check policy.
A statement identifying the days and hours of operation for the applicant.
A description of the geographic area to be served.

Written notice to the director within ten days of any change in the information given in the license application under (B)(3), or any other change that would make the submitted information inaccurate.
The chief administrator or designee requests that the superintendent conduct a criminal records check on each applicant for a direct care position.

The chief administrator or designee conducts a criminal background check on direct-care employees. For employees hired before 1/1/2008 it is no later than 30 days after the anniversary of the hire date and at least every five years. For employees hired on or after 1/1/2008 it is no later than 30 days after the fifth anniversary of the hire date and at least every five years.

Residency requirement: if the applicant cannot show five years of Ohio residency, or an FBI check within that period, the chief administrator requests that the superintendent obtain FBI information. The agency may request FBI information even if the applicant does meet the residency requirement.

Notification to the applicant or employee that fingerprint impressions are required and a criminal records check will be conducted. The notice must also cover any fee under (E)(2) and any fingerprinting fees authorized under ORC 109.572(C)(2).

Investigation fee: the agency pays BCI the prescribed fee for each check. It may charge the applicant a fee up to that amount only if it gives notice at the time of the initial application and Medicaid does not reimburse the fee.
Criminal records check forms: provide the prescribed forms and fingerprint impression sheet (or instructions), obtain the completed forms, and forward them to the superintendent.
An applicant or employee who fails to complete the forms or provide fingerprint impressions shall not be employed in any position for which a check is required.
Reverification of a criminal records check completed within the previous twelve months may be requested and accepted.

Exception: the agency need not request a check on an applicant referred by an employment service if the service confirms the database review and a criminal records check within one year, and both reports show no disqualifying offense.
Written instructions any individual may use to obtain payment for loss due to theft or property damage caused by the provider or the provider's employee.
Incident reporting: a written or electronic policy on documenting incidents that complies with paragraph (B)(3)(b) of the rule.

APS reporting: report any reasonable cause to believe an individual suffered abuse, neglect or exploitation to the local adult protective services program under ORC 5101.63. Also notify ODA or its designee within one business day.

Significant changes: notify ODA or its designee no later than one business day after becoming aware of a significant change affecting the individual's service needs or safety. The listed changes are (i) not providing an authorized service at the authorized time, (ii) the individual moving, (iii) repeated refusal of services, (iv) any incident subject to rule 5160-44-05, and (v) any other significant change in the individual's status or environment.
Notify ODA or its designee of any change in telephone number, mailing address or email address within seven days.
Last day of service: give the individual and ODA's designee written notice at least thirty days before the last day of service, except in the listed circumstances.
Confidentiality: the provider is subject to state and federal confidentiality laws (ORC 5160.45 to 5160.481, 42 CFR 431.300 to 431.307, 45 CFR parts 160, 162 and 164).
The provider shall supervise the provider's volunteers.

Ethical, professional, respectful and legal service standards: the provider shall not engage in unethical, unprofessional, disrespectful or illegal behavior. Items (a) to (n) cover alcohol, drugs, gifts and tips, sexual conduct, leaving the home, failing to cooperate with ODA, distracting activities, abuse or distress (including social media photos), personal relationships, decision-making roles, selling to or buying from the individual, use of the individual's food or property, taking the individual to the business site, and conflicts of interest.
Records retention: service records for six years after payment and until reviews and audits are resolved. Qualification records for the duration of certification or employment plus six years.

Policies: the agency provider shall have written policies, bylaws or articles of incorporation (or an electronic record of them) that include requirements for its employees to provide services in a manner compliant with paragraph (B)(8) of the rule.
Availability and staffing: accept a referral only if there are adequate staffing levels of PCAs and PCA supervisors to provide the hours authorized for each individual.
The PCA receives supervision from an RN or LPN under the direction of an RN during all hours PCAs are scheduled to work.
The provider shall maintain a back-up plan for providing personal care when no PCA or PCA supervisor is available.

PCA initial qualifications: (i) STNA, (ii) Medicare home health aide standards, (iii) previous experience, (iv) vocational programs, or (v) other programs with at least 30 hours of training covering the topics in (v)(b)(i)-(x).

Orientation before direct in-person contact. It must address (i) the provider's expectations of employees, (ii) ethical standards under rule 173-39-02, (iii) an overview of personnel policies, (iv) the organization and lines of communication of the agency, (v) incident-reporting procedures, (vi) emergency procedures, and (vii) standard precautions for infection control.
Additional training and competency evaluation if the PCA will perform activities for which the PCA was not trained or evaluated.
In-service training: each PCA completes six hours of ODA-approved in-service training every twelve months (ORC 173.525). Agency- and program-specific orientation do not count toward the six hours.

Verification of PCA qualifications: retain certificates of completion, or record the school or organization, course name, dates and hours. Also retain the nurse aide registry search results for STNAs and the previous-employment records for the experience pathway.
PCA supervisor qualifications: only an RN, or an LPN under the direction of an RN, may qualify as a PCA supervisor.

PCA supervisor visits: an initial in-person visit to define expected activities and develop a written or electronic activity plan. Subsequent visits are at least every sixty days, with provision for telephone or video visits if at least two in-person visits occur per year. Each visit is documented in the individual's record.
Provider policies: the provider shall develop, implement, comply with and maintain written or electronic policies on all of the following topics.
Job descriptions for each position.
Retaining records on how each PCA meets the qualifications in paragraph (C)(3) of the rule.

Service verification: for each episode retain (i) service date, (ii) PCA arrival time, (iii) PCA departure time, (iv) description of activities provided, (v) name of each PCA in contact with the individual, (vi) unique identifier of each PCA, and (vii) unique identifier of the individual. The provider is subject to Chapter 5160-32 (EVV) and ORC 121.36.

official.notes: No single ODH policy checklist or form exists for the nonmedical home health services license. The ODH page (last dated 11/17/2022) only requires the application, the $250 fee, the primary owner's fingerprint card and, for new providers, a $20,000 surety bond. I could not open the ODH application PDF, so the item list comes from the controlling rule, OAC 3701-60-03(B). For the ODH license, submit the application packet with (1) a list of nonmedical services and related policies and procedures, (2) the written criminal records check policy, (3) a statement of days and hours of operation, and (4) a description of the geographic area served. These are items (B)(3)(d), (g), (h) and (i). Items (B)(3)(d) to (k) are waived for providers holding ODA certification (3701-60-03(E)). Items (B)(3)(d) to (i) are waived for providers accredited by ACHC, CHAP, the Joint Commission or another approved national organization (3701-60-03(F)). For ODA PASSPORT certification, ODA does not publish a policy-manual checklist. It requires written or electronic policies on job descriptions and PCA qualification records (173-39-02.11(C)(5)), an incident-documentation policy (173-39-02(A)(7)), written theft or property-damage claim instructions (173-39-02(A)(5)(b)), and policies, bylaws or articles that bind employees to the 173-39-02(B)(8) conduct standards (173-39-02(C)(1)(c)). Organize the manual to follow these rule paragraph numbers so a reviewer can map each policy to its citation. The ODM rules (OAC 5160-46-04 and 5160-58-04) were not fetched in this pass, so no items from them are listed. The ODA certification rules also call for an organization table, ownership disclosures and attestations, but these are disclosure paperwork and not policy content, so they are excluded. Where an item above is a duty and not a literally required 'policy', the manual should still address it. Examples are the 3701-60-06 criminal records check steps, the 173-39-02(B)(3) reporting duties and the 173-39-02.11(C)(3)-(4) training and supervision rules.
